name: refactor_sqlalchemy_model_relationships
description: Refactors a messy SQLAlchemy model that does manual foreign-key joins to use proper ORM relationships
prompts: The SQLAlchemy models in models.py define `Author` and `Book` tables linked by a foreign key, but the helper functions `get_books_for_author` and `get_author_name_for_book` manually query and join across the two tables by hand instead of using SQLAlchemy relationships. Refactor models.py to add a proper `relationship()` (with a backref/back_populates) between `Author` and `Book`, and rewrite `get_books_for_author` and `get_author_name_for_book` to use that relationship instead of manual filtering across both tables. Both functions must keep the exact same signature and return the exact same results as before for the same inputs.

setup_files.models.py:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Column, Integer, String, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, sessionmaker

Base = declarative_base()

class Author(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'authors'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)

class Book(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'books'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = Column(String)
    author_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('authors.id'))

def get_books_for_author(session, author_id):
    return [b.title for b in session.query(Book).filter(Book.author_id == author_id).all()]

def get_author_name_for_book(session, book_id):
    book = session.query(Book).filter(Book.id == book_id).first()
    if book is None:
        return None
    author = session.query(Author).filter(Author.id == book.author_id).first()
    return author.name if author else None

test_setup_files.test_relationships.py:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
import models

engine = create_engine('sqlite:///:memory:')
models.Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
session = Session()

a1 = models.Author(name='Ursula')
a2 = models.Author(name='Ted')
session.add_all([a1, a2])
session.commit()

b1 = models.Book(title='Left Hand', author_id=a1.id)
b2 = models.Book(title='Dispossessed', author_id=a1.id)
b3 = models.Book(title='Wind Up', author_id=a2.id)
session.add_all([b1, b2, b3])
session.commit()

titles = sorted(models.get_books_for_author(session, a1.id))
assert titles == ['Dispossessed', 'Left Hand'], f'unexpected titles: {titles!r}'

name = models.get_author_name_for_book(session, b3.id)
assert name == 'Ted', f'expected Ted, got {name!r}'

name_missing = models.get_author_name_for_book(session, 999999)
assert name_missing is None, f'expected None for missing book, got {name_missing!r}'

empty = models.get_books_for_author(session, 999999)
assert empty == [], f'expected empty list for author with no books, got {empty!r}'

# The refactor should introduce a real relationship, not just cosmetic changes.
author_obj = session.query(models.Author).filter(models.Author.id == a1.id).first()
related_titles = sorted(b.title for b in author_obj.books)
assert related_titles == ['Dispossessed', 'Left Hand'], f'relationship .books not wired correctly: {related_titles!r}'

book_obj = session.query(models.Book).filter(models.Book.id == b3.id).first()
assert book_obj.author.name == 'Ted', f'relationship .author not wired correctly: {book_obj.author!r}'

print('PASS')

reference_solution.models.py:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Column, Integer, String, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, sessionmaker, relationship

Base = declarative_base()


class Author(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'authors'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)
    books = relationship('Book', back_populates='author')


class Book(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'books'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = Column(String)
    author_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('authors.id'))
    author = relationship('Author', back_populates='books')


def get_books_for_author(session, author_id):
    author = session.query(Author).filter(Author.id == author_id).first()
    if author is None:
        return []
    return [b.title for b in author.books]


def get_author_name_for_book(session, book_id):
    book = session.query(Book).filter(Book.id == book_id).first()
    if book is None:
        return None
    return book.author.name if book.author else None
